best_parts: node open: 'See what you already hold' opener with ask_confidence on the first psoas/obturator/Rovsing probe; a clean diagnostic start for a tired learner
nodes p2_t3 and p2_t1: every wrong option carries a tempting line, a refutation, and a sure_note; the direction probe is the best Rovsing-reversal test across the three variants
node p6_tb: names the exact wrong weighting (rebound scored 2) and points to the blood count as the second 2-point item
flaws: node p2_t1 (and the same option in variant b's rov_t1): 'Extending the right hip causes pain in the right iliac fossa' has no pressure word, so a learner who knows only 'Rovsing = pressure' drops it by form; it is dominated (DP2)

node p6_hint: 'Think about which items are the most specific: the appendix itself, and the body's response to it in the blood' nearly gives the two 2-point items and reinforces the specificity model that TR6 names as the error

nodes p5_t, p6_ta, p6_tb, p8_partial: wrong feedback offers only 'Try again', so a tired learner cannot move on without the right tap; O8 looks only at the female differential (p8_ok), not look-alikes by child or adult group

best_parts: node case: a 24-year-old with 18 hours of central pain that moved to the RIF; a real clinical moment that frames the psoas choice (R7)
node ttr_ok: look-alikes by group (children, women, adults) with K58, K59, K60; covers O8 on every path, because every route reaches this node
node cl: a cold which-is-not probe with no hint option that re-tests TR1 and TR2 in exam form; obt_t1 and pos_mech_t1 offer 'Next' after a wrong tap, so a tired learner is not stuck
flaws: nodes obt_t1, obt_t3, pos_mech_t1, pos_mech_t2, rov_t1, rov_t3, alv2_t9, alv2_t6, cl_t1, cl_t2: no sure_note, so a confident error gets no hypercorrection line; obt_t1, obt_t3, rov_t3, alv2_t9, alv2_t6 use 'Wrong:' as an opener, which the voice rule discourages
node rov_t1: 'Pain in the right iliac fossa on extending the right hip' has no pressure word, so it is dominated by form and no one holding the Rovsing model is tempted by it (DP2)

node alv_hint: 'Only two items score 2 ... Look for the local sign at the appendix and the one blood result' almost names the answer; also the key 'RIF tenderness and leucocytosis' is the shortest option on alv, a form cue

best_parts: node a_t1 and its a_why: short tempting-then-refute feedback with an agency 'Show me why' that leads to one clear re-explanation
node g_why: groups of RIF look-alikes (child, woman, adult) in one message pair, covering O8 at the right depth
nodes c_probe to g_probe: the tightest one-idea-per-node run in the three variants; a tired learner gets a probe, feedback and the next probe with little load
flaws: Rovsing direction is never probed: TR3 (the reversal error) appears only as a recognition distractor (a_t3, b_probe), with no predict-then-show or contrast probe; a learner who reverses Rovsing is never caught on this path (R2, R9)
node e_hint: 'Think about which are local signs at the site, and which one is a blood test' points straight at the two 2-point items; the hint leaks the answer
node a_probe: the key 'Extension of the right hip' is the shortest option, a form cue; no cold probe in this segment; no which-is-not form in the exam-trap sense

merge_ideas: b's 'case' clinical opener with a's 'open' confidence-led opener, so the first probe is both a real patient and a what-do-you-hold check
a's full sure_note coverage on every wrong tap, added to b's obt/rov/alv2/cl wrong nodes, which currently lack it
a's direction probe (p2) for Rovsing's reversal placed after b's rov node, closing the gap in variant c
b's 'Next' escape after a wrong tap on the mid-path probes (obt, pos_mech), with a's delayed retest in cl kept as the check
b's ttr_ok group look-alikes reached on every path, plus c's g_why wording for the child and adult groups
c's tight one-idea-per-node sequence (c_probe to g_probe) as the spine, with a's explain-then-probe rhythm around the Rovsing direction
